summary: The FAIR Exams Act establishes new procedures and timelines for the federal examination of financial institutions. It creates the Office of Independent Examination Review to handle complaints and appeals concerning examination reports, sets deadlines for regulatory agencies to complete examinations and exit interviews, gives financial institutions the right to an independent review of material supervisory determinations, and prohibits retaliation against institutions that exercise these appellate rights.

affected_groups.effect: Receive clearer deadlines for examinations and reports, gain the right to independently appeal material supervisory determinations, and are protected from retaliation by regulators.

Must adhere to statutory timelines for examinations, exit interviews, and guidance requests, fund the new Office of Independent Examination Review, and comply with binding independent review decisions.

key_provisions: Establishes the Office of Independent Examination Review within the Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council, governed by a 3-member board appointed by the President.
Requires federal financial regulatory agencies to complete examinations within 270 days and conduct exit interviews within 30 days of completion, subject to written extensions.
Grants financial institutions the right to obtain an independent review of a material supervisory determination contained in a final examination report.
Sets strict timelines for agencies to respond to requests for written guidance, permissions, and interpretations.
Prohibits federal regulatory agencies from retaliating against financial institutions for exercising their appeal rights.
Provides financial institutions with the right to appeal final independent review decisions to a U.S. Court of Appeals.
missing_information: Specific funding amounts or budgetary figures for the operation of the Office of Independent Examination Review beyond the requirement that costs be split among regulatory agencies.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The FAIR Exams Act establishes new procedures and timelines for the federal examination of financial institutions. It creates the Office of Independent Examination Review to handle complaints and appeals concerning examination reports, sets deadlines for regulatory agencies to complete examinations and exit interviews, gives financial institutions the right to an independent review of material supervisory determinations, and prohibits retaliation against institutions that exercise these appellate rights.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates an independent appeals process and enforces strict statutory deadlines for federal financial regulators, altering how bank and credit union examinations are conducted and reviewed. The potential impact is evaluated as 75 (substantial) because it creates a new federal oversight body and modifies regulatory examination procedures across the financial sector.
